decision: Complete the descriptive study and defer any crossing-composition entry filter. The 20 higher-contribution trades have 70% wins and +21.12 mean net bps; four lower-contribution trades have 50% wins and +53.06 mean net bps, all before the extension partition. Neither direction is supported as a live filter; do not sweep the threshold.
falsifier: Changed source hashes or a baseline mismatch invalidate technical reproduction. An independently specified forward sample with both groups represented, stable cost-adjusted differences across contexts, and full chronological entry-occupancy simulation would update the decision to defer a filter.
hypothesis: A fixed price-contribution split can describe differences between historical SPCX long recoveries without changing the baseline strategy. Any relative profitability prediction remains low confidence.
limitations: Previously screened 48-day evaluation; hypothesis motivated by two later observed live entries. Not untouched validation.
Only four lower-contribution executed longs, all in development; none in the later partition.
Higher-contribution win rate and lower-contribution mean return do not establish a causal ranking; ATR, trend context, time concentration and winner concentration differ.
Baseline candle fills and slippage stress do not establish current venue depth, mark-trigger paths, latency or achievable live returns.
Fully held candle excursions plus fills are lower bounds; the exit candle is excluded because intrabar ordering is unknown.
Group P&L is not a filtered strategy result; changing prior entries changes later position occupancy.
No new live strategy, settings, orders, deployment or process changes. The locked SNDK/Brent forward experiment was not inspected.
